sources.entry: Offen - Fair, lightweight and open web analytics tool. Gain insights while your users have full access to their data. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Offen Fair Web Analytics is a self-hosted, lightweight web analytics tool where end users can opt in to tracking and access their own data.
summary.what_it_does: Offen is a self-hosted web analytics tool that collects usage data only after visitors actively opt in via a consent banner. The README says usage data is encrypted end-to-end, with clients encrypting data in the browser before it is sent to the server. Operators can analyze multiple websites within one installation, share website accounts within teams, and filter metrics by URL, location, referrer, UTM parameters, landing pages and exit pages. Users can view their own data with explanations of metrics, and delete their data or opt out at any time. The README states that user data is stored for 6 months and then deleted, and that only first-party cookies are used. It can run as a single binary or Docker image, with optional automatic SSL certificate handling and SQLite as an alternative to a dedicated database.
use_cases: letting users see and delete their own tracking data
tracking UTM campaigns and landing pages
how_to_run: curl | bash (one-off demo installation, per README; the URL is missing from the README text)
Download the single binary or pull the Docker image and run it on your server
Development: install docker and the compose plugin, then git clone git@github.com:offen/offen.git
notable: End-to-end encryption of usage data, encrypted in the browser before reaching the server
Opt-in consent model with users able to review and delete their own data
Single binary or Docker deployment with optional automatic SSL certificates
Customizable consent banner in color, shape and basic font
Available in English, French, German, Portuguese, Spanish and Vietnamese
caveats: Development setup requires docker and the compose plugin
Detailed setup docs are on an external docs site; the README omits the links
Mixed licensing: the logo and icon are CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0, not Apache-2.0
